| τὸν καὶ νεικείων προσέφη ξανθὸς Μενέλαος (23.438, whole-line speech introduction) | "Him, rebuking, addressed fair-haired Menelaus:" | "Fair-haired Menelaus said to him, rebuking him:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); καί left untranslated; follows the table's ἐπιθαρσύνων … προσέφη ξανθὸς Μενέλαος (4.183) and νεικείων "rebuking" (2.221) |
| τὸν δ’ αἰσχρῶς ἐνένιπεν Ὀϊλῆος ταχὺς Αἴας (23.473, whole-line speech introduction) | "And him shamefully rebuked swift Ajax, son of Oileus:" | "Swift Ajax, son of Oileus, rebuked him rudely:" | "answered", "taunted"; ἐνίπτω "rebuke" (15.546), Ὀϊλῆος ταχὺς Αἴας "swift Ajax, son of Oileus" (table); αἰσχρῶς "shamefully" in `l`, "rudely" in `i` |
| Ἀντίλοχος δ’ ἵπποισιν ἐκέκλετο πατρὸς ἑοῖο (23.402, whole-line speech introduction) | "And Antilochus called out to the horses of his own father:" | "Antilochus called out to his father’s horses:" | "urged", "shouted to"; ἐκέκλετο "called out" (6.66, 23.442) |
| ἐριζέμεν … οὔ τι κελεύω (23.404) | "I do not at all bid you to quarrel" | "I do not tell you to compete" | "contend", "rival", "strive"; `l` keeps the table's ἐριζέμεναι "to quarrel" (2.214, 21.185); `i` departs to "compete" because "quarrel with horses" does not read as a race |
| τὼ δέ οἱ ὄσσε δακρυόφι πλῆσθεν, θαλερὴ δέ οἱ ἔσχετο φωνή (23.396–397) | "and his two eyes were filled with tears, and his full voice was checked." | "and his eyes filled with tears, and his strong voice was choked." | Odyssey (odyssey-020) wording, with "her" turned to "his" because the one weeping is Eumelus |
| ἀμφήριστον (23.382; rare, "disputed on both sides") | "disputed" | "left the race in dispute" | "a dead heat" (a gloss, in the note), "doubtful", "a draw"; ἀμφί + ἐρίζω-type compound, kept to the sense "disputed" |
| ἐλεφηράμενος (23.388; rare) | "cheating" | "cheating" | "tricking", "deceiving", "mocking"; ἐλεφαίρομαι "cheat, deceive" |
| ἐβλάφθησαν · ἔβλαβεν (23.387, 23.461) | "were hindered" · "were hindered" | "were hampered" · "have come to grief" | "harmed" (kept for the Odyssey's βλάπτω "harm" where a person is hurt), "damaged"; βλάπτω "hinder, hamper" of horses and chariots |
| ἠρώησαν ὀπίσσω · ἐξηρώησαν (23.433, 23.468) | "drew back, behind" · "drew back out" | "drew back behind" · "bolted off the course" | "held back" (kept for ἐρύκω and the table's 13.776 usage), "swerved"; ἐρωέω "draw back" as in the table (2.179, 13.776), with ἐκ- in the second |
| ἀποκηδήσαντε (23.413, dual participle) | "through slackness" | "if we grow slack" | "being careless", "losing heart"; ἀποκηδέω "stop caring, grow careless" |
| ἄεθλον (23.413, 23.441; the prize, not the contest) | "contest-prize" | "prize" | "contest" (reserved for the Odyssey's ἄεθλος); follows the table's ἄεθλα (23.259) "contest-prizes … prizes" |
| ἁματροχιάς (23.422; rare, "running together of wheels") | "wheel-clashes" | "clashes of wheels" | "wheel-tracks", "ruts"; ἅμα + τροχός, the note explains it |
| ῥωχμός · στεῖνος (23.420, 23.419) | "gully" · "narrow place" | "gully" · "narrow place" | "ravine", "ditch", "pass"; στεινωπός "narrow" (23.416) is the adjective from the same root |
| ἄνεχ’ ἵππους (23.426) | "hold the horses up" | "rein in your horses" | "hold back" (kept for ἐρύκω), "restrain"; ἀνέχω "hold up" |
| ὅσσα δὲ δίσκου οὖρα κατωμαδίοιο πέλονται (23.431) | "as great as the range of a discus hurled from the shoulder is" | "as far as a discus carries when … thrown from the shoulder" | "the length of a discus-throw"; οὖρα "range, reach of a cast" |
| πεπνῦσθαι (23.440) | "that you had sense" | "you had any sense" | "were wise", "were clever"; πέπνυμαι "be sensible"; the plural φάμεν gives "we … said" |
| ὁμοκλητήρ (23.452) | "the man shouting" | "the driver shouting" | "the shouter" (as an agent noun); ὁμοκλάω "shout at" per the table |
| ἐπεὶ μένος ἔλλαβε θυμόν (23.468) | "when might took hold of their spirit" | "when their wild strength took hold of their spirit" | "courage", "fury"; μένος "might" (the table), θυμός "spirit" |
| λαβρεύεαι · λαβραγόρην (23.474, 23.478, 23.479) | "you babble" · "a babbler" | "you babble" · "a loose talker" | "rave", "prattle"; λάβρος "violent" (16.385) is the root, the English keeps the wildness of the talk |
| εὔληρα (23.481; a poetic word for "reins") | "reins" | "reins" | "good reins", "fine reins" (the first part is not certain); ἡνία "reins" |
